stories.headline: Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained
stories.summary: Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk -- it is unofficially the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix, but it is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.
stories.body:
Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk. Look at the calendar and you'll see the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix. The only catch? It is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.

You don't have to be a geography buff to know those two places are not the same, nor are they close on the map. The bizarre event all comes down to global politics and is part of a wider situation that has left the destination of F1's season-ending races -- events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- uncertain, too.

Here's everything you need to know about F1's first "Middle Eastern" race of the year, and the current status of the final two races in the region which are meant to close the 2026 season.

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

First things first, what are we calling this race?
Amusingly, perhaps slightly farcically, F1's next race will be called the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, held on Oct. 4, sandwiched between events in Baku and Singapore. It means another triple header on the calendar, with the season already due (as it stands) to feature Austin-Mexico City-Brazil, a gap, then Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi.

While a slightly ridiculous naming convention, the event does mark a welcome and surprise return for the hugely popular Sepang circuit, which last hosted a race in 2017 after 18 years on the calendar. F1 understands the official flag next to the event will be Bahrain's, and the winner of the race will be considered to be a winner of the Bahrain Grand Prix in F1's official record books.

What national anthem will play before the event?
Exact plans remain to be seen, though sources have told ESPN that pre-race grid plans feature both the Bahrain and Malaysian flags, while Bahrain's national band is also in Malaysia for the event.

Once the Bahrain band has done playing the Bahrain anthem, those on the grid and in the grandstands lining the start-finish straight will be treated to a flyover by a Gulf Air Dreamliner, which has also been flown over specifically for this event. That's been a regular fixture of the Bahrain Grand Prix.

What happened to Bahrain's original race?
The decision not to hold races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in April was a by-product of ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, triggered by a wave of attacks launched on Iran by the United States and Israel in March. That saw a number of countries in the region struck by Iran in response -- including Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. Bahrain's capital Manama was hit just weeks after it had hosted preseason testing.
As a result, F1 cancelled what would have been back-to-back races, the Bahrain Grand Prix on April 12 and Jeddah's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix on April 19. That left a four-week gap in the calendar between the Japanese Grand Prix and the Miami Grand Prix without a race. Importantly, at the time F1 made it clear the door was open for both events to happen later in the year should the situation in the region cool down.

Was rescheduling either event a realistic option?
Originally, F1 hoped it might be able to reschedule one or both events if and when the situation in the region cooled. Bahrain naturally was the easier option -- it's a permanent facility and, having hosted preseason and in anticipation of the event that should have taken place in April, some freight remains there which never left the nation state. That meant there was automatically a lot more flexibility around rearranging Bahrain if the opportunity had presented itself. As for Saudi Arabia, that was more complicated -- the Jeddah event is a street circuit around the city, for one thing, and street circuits naturally require a bit more lead-time in terms of preparation.

Sources have told ESPN that while Bahrain were happy to host an event wherever possible, Saudi's organisers had been set on rescheduling their race as a season-ending race. Even without a massive de-escalation in the Middle East, that presented big issues -- the season is already due to finish on Dec. 6 in Abu Dhabi. To avoid an unprecedented four straight races, a Saudi race would likely have needed to be held in the middle of December or nearer Christmas time, which has never happened before. Then there's Abu Dhabi's place as the season-ender -- the UAE venue has been the long-time finale event and pays a premium for the privilege. Sources have told ESPN Abu Dhabi was not thrilled at the idea of letting a regional rival take that from them. All of that is irrelevant now, anyway -- Abu Dhabi and Qatar's races both look set to be cancelled due to the same conflict (more on that below).

Why did Malaysia help Bahrain out?
It might seem like a strange link-up on the surface, but the two nations actually share a close diplomatic relationship stretching back to 1974. Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Malaysia King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar reportedly have a strong personal rapport. Sources have told ESPN the plan was first discussed in a conversation between the pair and a plan quickly unfolded from there. Bahrain had a race to reschedule and Malaysia had a beloved circuit completely free to step in. Malaysia offered to split the cost with Bahrain and it was seen as a win-win -- a good way to mark strong diplomatic ties between the two nations, while Bahrain gets to say it retained its grand prix on the 2026 calendar and Sepang gets the feel-good rub of stepping in and helping Bahrain and Formula 1 out in an hour of need.

Why was Bahrain so keen to hold a race, even if not on its own circuit?
Bahrain has been invested in F1 for a long time now. It first hosted a race in 2004 and has become a mainstay on the calendar, often as the season-opener, as well as becoming a regular and reliable preseason test venue. The nation state is also deeply intertwined with the sport -- Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund, Mumtalakat Holding Company, is majority owner of the McLaren team and full owner of the wider McLaren Group.

The scale of its involvement in F1 is far deeper than is currently the case in Saudi. But it wasn't just Bahrain that felt a need to get something sorted. The rearrangement is big from a contractual perspective for Formula 1 as well. The sport's commercial agreement with its 11 teams and its global broadcasters says the season cannot drop below 22 races -- should that ever happen, the financial cost for the sport would be severe. Bahrain and Saudi had already both been cancelled -- with Qatar and Abu Dhabi both likely to be canned at the end of the season, the sport effectively needed to find two replacements in quick time. Malaysia and Bahrain doing a deal meant F1 only had to find one race to finish the season with, should those other two events be cancelled as expected. As we will come to, easier options in Europe existed to fill a one-race gap.

What was Sepang like, and why did it stop hosting F1 in the first place?
Sepang enjoyed 18 years as a Formula 1 host between 1999 and 2017 and quickly established itself as a popular venue, with drivers loving its fast, flowing corners, while it boasts numerous places to overtake. Sepang actually was unlucky in the timing of its departure from the calendar -- Formula 1 was in a much less lucrative place at the time.

Liberty Media had only just taken over with a grand plan for the sport's growth, which has come to pass in the years since Covid. In 2017 things were not quite so rosy as they are now -- then-CEO of Sepang, Razlan Razali, told Reuters at the time: "It's hard to sell this kind of event and to get bums on the seats. It's not worth the investment at the moment." Of course, F1 has enjoyed stratospheric growth since the pandemic and most races are easy sellouts, with huge revenues and 11 teams all worth north of $1 billion (£753 million). Hindsight is 20-20, as they say.

Does this one-off return make Malaysia a candidate to host events again in the future?
It's hard to say for now. This event certainly can't hurt, and it's clear the event is in F1's good graces at the moment for stepping in. But it's not simply a case of it being fast-tracked to the front of the line for a future event. F1's calendar is already jam-packed at 24 events -- next year Portugal and Türkiye return, and F1 boss Stefano Domenicali often says there is a queue of potential venues waiting for a spot to open up, with the sport keen to prioritise an event in Africa in future if a viable venue materialises. Then there's Singapore, which may not be thrilled at the prospect of hosting a race so close to a neighbour every year. When Sepang was a regular host, Singapore and Malaysia were often next to each other on the calendar, but rarely just a week apart.
Isn't F1's season finishing in the Middle East as it stands? What about those two races?
As it stands, yes, although it seems likely that will change in the coming weeks after F1 bosses were told that they can expect a final decision by mid-October. The calendar as it stands says Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6 will close the season, but F1 has been delaying a decision on both events as it monitors the situation in the region and there was hope the events could both go ahead as planned.

The World Endurance Championship, the series which holds the famous Le Mans 24 Hours, has already cancelled a race in Qatar that was due to be held in November. Sources have told ESPN that Italian circuit Imola will hold the season-ending race should Qatar and Abu Dhabi be cancelled. In that scenario, the race would take place on Dec. 6, the existing spot for Abu Dhabi's race. While eyebrows in the paddock have been raised at hosting a race in northern Italy in December, logistically the race presents an easy option, with all 11 teams based in Europe.

- Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

Is Imola really the only option to step in?
Many in F1 have wondered the same thing, but the circuit has only just dropped off the calendar as a grand prix host, so its infrastructure is in place. Weather is far from ideal, with sunlight at a minimum and snow a regular feature, but the circuit has close ties to the sport which probably helped shuffle the historic venue to the front of the line -- it is the hometown of F1 CEO Domenicali and Ferrari's unofficial home race, given its close proximity to Ferrari's Maranello headquarters. Still, others wondered if other venues might be more appropriate.

F1 is due to race in Las Vegas the weekend before Thanksgiving, leaving many to speculate whether F1 could stay in America and race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas (COTA), which is already hosting a race on Oct. 24. However, COTA does not appear to have put itself forward nor does it appear to have been asked by F1 to stand in. Portugal's Portimao circuit was also floated as an option, but stepping in to host an event in December would have threatened the timeline of the renovations and upgrades the venue is doing in order to host a race next season. Imola, which dropped off the calendar after its 2025 race, has therefore emerged as the likely season-ender.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad. O'Reilly returned to Manchester for further treatment before England played Croatia.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

Christos Tzolis (Arsenal)

The Greece winger limped out of his side's draw against the Netherlands after just 18 minutes.

Tzolis pulled his shirt over his head and looked upset as he left the match early.

He represents another headache for Arsenal after Kai Havertz's prior injury for Germany.

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Dodgers' Ohtani admits he won't be fully healthy in playoffs
stories.summary: Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani said the left knee and right biceps ailments that compromised him throughout the summer are issues he's "just going to have to manage" in the postseason.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Dodgers' two-way star Shohei Ohtani called the past few days "very productive" and believes his swing is "in a better place" heading into a National League Division Series showdown against the Atlanta Braves that begins Saturday.

But Ohtani won't be fully healthy then and perhaps at any point this postseason. The left knee and right biceps ailments that compromised him throughout the summer will linger into the fall, Ohtani and Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Friday.

"As of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage," Ohtani said through an interpreter.

Knee and biceps injuries finally sent Ohtani to the injured list in early September after a 14-game stretch during which he compiled seven hits and 22 strikeouts. Ohtani returned with five regular-season games left and was inconsistent, putting together an encouraging stretch against the San Diego Padres and an overwhelming one against the San Francisco Giants.

Ohtani took batting practice on the field during workouts Tuesday and Wednesday, a rarity for him, and Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates said those sessions were "as good as we've seen it this year as far as the way the ball was coming off and the way he was getting his move off."

Bates provided some proof of that.

"He did hit a couple balls up off the scoreboard," he said.

Ohtani also had three plate appearances against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in a prolonged simulated game Wednesday, worked out inside Thursday and came onto the field for three rounds of outdoor batting practice around 6 p.m. PT on Friday. Moments later, he had two at-bats against right-hander Emmet Sheehan, striking out before hitting a line drive to right field.

"Shohei's not 100%, but he's going to be in the lineup," Roberts said, adding that veteran first baseman Freddie Freeman also isn't fully healthy, among others. "I think that most players that are performing now are not 100%. Obviously with Shohei, it's a bigger deal because of the player, but there's a lot of players that are not 100%, and they've just got to manage it."

Despite being compromised for much of the past three months, Ohtani finished the year batting .275/.377/.512 with 30 home runs and 11 stolen bases and is likely to finish second to Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong in NL MVP voting. Ohtani also went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts, but he didn't pitch after July 3 and had essentially been ruled out of pitching by Labor Day. Ohtani went on the IL thereafter.

"During the IL, I pretty much knew I wasn't going to pitch the rest of the season," Ohtani said. "So, I did focus on just the hitting aspect of the game and coming to understanding and wanting to execute and try new things when I came back. So, those were the things that I really took the IL time to think through what I wanted to try when I was back in action."

Ohtani had several hard-hit balls upon returning from the IL, notably an opposite-field double off a 103 mph fastball from star Padres closer Mason Miller. But Ohtani ultimately went 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts in his last five regular-season games, and by the end, Roberts noticed him being overanxious, trying too hard to get acclimated to major league pitching with limited time.

Ohtani, 32, said he still has to make "little tweaks here and there" with his swing before feeling ready for Game 1.

He downplayed having limited playing time before then.

"Whether I have a lot of at-bats or not, I can figure out how I feel, especially in my setup," Ohtani said. "So, that's something I was able to kind of see. But I do want to get into the postseason, feel the atmosphere and again kind of recalibrate what I have to."

stories.headline: MMA 30 under 30: Champions Joshua Van and Usman Nurmagomedov lead
stories.summary: The future is now! Joshua Van, Usman Nurmagomedov and more championship-caliber fighters top 30 under 30 list.
stories.body:
ESPN's yearly list of the top 30 fighters under age 30 can be characterized as a look into the future. These are the young fighters who presumably will take over once the sport's top veterans move on.

But this year's ranking is not merely forward thinking.

Consider that the top two fighters -- Joshua Van in the UFC and Usman Nurmagomedov in the PFL -- aren't rising prospects. They are defending champions. No. 3 Ilia Topuria is a former UFC champion. And Natalia Silva, who sits at No. 9, will go for the vacant women's flyweight title this weekend at UFC 332. In MMA, it seems, "the future is now" is not simply a catchy slogan.

There also are up-and-comers in these rankings, as there are every year, and many who have appeared before are now in different positions, as a year's worth of fight results dictates.

Our panel -- Brett Okamoto, Dre Waters, Jeff Wagenheim, Andrew Davis, James Regan, Sam Bruce, James Dielhenn, Marcus Vanderberg and Alecia Hamm -- selected fighters based on their achievements this year and their potential. Okamoto, Waters and Wagenheim provide breakdowns of the top 30 under 30.

1. Joshua Van

UFC men's flyweight champion

Age: 24

2025 rank: 3

It takes a remarkable athlete to lead this type of list -- but to lead it at 24 years old is just absurd. Van is arguably the purest talent the sport has seen in years. No one could have predicted at the start of 2025, when his ascension truly took off, that he would end the year as ESPN's best breakout fighter. He is undeniably the best active flyweight on the planet and has the personality and charisma to match. Sean O'Malley recently proclaimed on his YouTube channel that Van will go down as the "greatest flyweight of all time." After Van's second win over former longtime champion Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331, who wants to disagree? -- Okamoto

2. Usman Nurmagomedov

PFL lightweight champion

Age: 28

2025 rank: 7

It's unusual for a fighter outside the UFC to establish himself as the best in his weight class, but that's exactly what Nurmagomedov has done with his perfect 21-0 record. It's not unreasonable to suggest Nurmagomedov would be favored against any other 155-pound fighter in the world, including top-ranked UFC lightweights Justin Gaethje, Arman Tsarukyan and Ilia Topuria. Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent, and his next move is one of the biggest questions in MMA this year. -- Okamoto

3. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 1

Topuria entered the year as the UFC lightweight champion, ESPN's top-ranked fighter under 30 and on the short list of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He got his first chance to defend the belt in a main event at the White House on June 14, but the challenger, Gaethje, handed him the first loss of his professional career, retiring him on the stool after four rounds. Despite the loss, Topuria remains one of MMA's best young fighters. -- Waters

4. Michael Morales

UFC welterweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 5

Fans love a good knockout, and Morales has handed out KOs regularly on his way to the welterweight title picture. Three consecutive first-round finishes have all the momentum on Morales's side, but he hasn't fought yet this year. He's on champion Islam Makhachev's radar as a future welterweight challenger, but he'll likely need one more win against a top contender to get his first title shot. -- Okamoto

5. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL women's flyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 2

One of the most destructive figures in women's MMA, Ditcheva is uniquely violent, boasting a 73% knockout rate in the PFL. The question isn't whether she can be a star, it's how big her star can become. With Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions acquiring the PFL going into 2027, we will find out what the ceiling is for Ditcheva's exposure. She is exactly the kind of marketable athlete MVP will get behind. -- Okamoto

6. Song Yadong

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 28

Song put two years of little activity behind him by fighting three times in the first eight months of 2026. He lost a tight decision to Sean O'Malley in January, but he bounced back in May against another champion, choking out Deiveson Figueiredo. But what elevated Song most on this list -- he was way down at No. 28 last year -- was his knockout of Umar Nurmagomedov in August. That stunning result boosted Song's stock as a men's bantamweight contender. Next up should be another ranked opponent, giving him an opportunity to build off of his recent success. -- Wagenheim

7. Josh Hokit

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Hokit's antics on the microphone may not have endeared him to UFC CEO Dana White, who said at UFC 331 that he doesn't like anything Hokit says. But the heavyweight's performance in his second year in the Octagon has skyrocketed him to the top of the division. "I say it all the time: I don't have to like you for you to thrive here and you to do well and be successful," White said of Hokit's ascension. With just four UFC fights under his belt -- three this year -- Hokit is set to challenge Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight championship in the main event at UFC 334 in November. Hokit, who earned a contract on Season 9 of "Dana White's Contender Series" just 13 months ago, already has beaten heavyweight stalwarts Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis in two of the more entertaining fights of the year. Ending 2026 with a UFC championship would be an impressive cap to his year. -- Waters

8. Ian Machado Garry

UFC welterweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 6

Love him or hate him, Machado Garry might be the best UFC welterweight not named Islam Makhachev. He took the pound-for-pound king five competitive rounds in August and is still in great position to accept some of the biggest fights available as he works his way back toward a second title shot. Machado Garry has said he believes that a loss to Makhachev will only make him better, and there are plenty of reasons to believe the 28-year-old's best is still in front of him. -- Okamoto

9. Natalia Silva

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 9

Silva might be a UFC champion by the end of the weekend. By winning 14 fights in a row, the past eight in the Octagon, she has been looking more and more like championship material. Her three most recent wins came against former titleholders Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva is poised to take over if she handles Wang Cong at UFC 332. Women's flyweight is a highly competitive division, with several pound-for-pound elites. It could be Silva's domain until someone figures out how to contend with her slick movement. -- Wagenheim

10. Quillan Salkilld

UFC lightweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: 23

Somehow, even in a division full of potential superstars, Australia's Salkilld has managed to stand out -- and not just because he has a great mustache. Salkilld's got a look and presence on social media that plays well with the UFC's fanbase, and he has substance to back up the flash. He is on a streak of five consecutive first-round finishes, including in his most recent win, in which he beat submission artist Mateusz Gamrot at his own game with a first-round rear-naked choke. Salkilld has that "it" factor, and if he keeps winning, he will collide with some of the sport's biggest names. -- Okamoto

11. Jean Silva

UFC featherweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 15

Silva was denied a higher-profile opportunity when his Noche UFC opponent, popular and flashy Yair Rodriguez, withdrew from last month's fight because of injury. Silva did not suffer a letdown against late replacement Jose Miguel Delgado, taking care of business by doing what he usually does: making the fight his showcase. The win was Silva's second in a row after a September 2025 knockout loss ended a 13-fight winning streak. Silva is building himself toward featherweight contention with an aggressive fighting style that is a dream for fans and a nightmare for opponents. -- Wagenheim

12. Tatsuro Taira

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 26

Last year's rank: 22

Taira won eight of his first nine UFC fights, a run of success capped by a knockout of former two-time men's flyweight champion Brandon Moreno in December. But it was a loss that drew more attention to him -- positive attention. Taira ended up being knocked out by current champion Joshua Van in a title fight in May, but it was a back-and-forth fight that lasted into the fifth round. Taira put the champ in trouble with eight takedowns and over 10 minutes of control time. It was fight of the night, keeping the Japanese fighter in the contender conversation. -- Wagenheim

13. Navajo Stirling

UFC light heavyweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

Entering 2026, all three of Stirling's UFC wins had come by unanimous decision, but that stretch seems like an anomaly now. Stirling earned a UFC contract via a second-round knockout on "Dana White's Contender Series" in 2024 and had knocked out three of his four professional opponents before that. He officially refound his finishing ways this year, winning each of his three fights by knockout, including a first-round TKO over former light heavyweight champion Jan Blachowicz in August. Stirling may not have opened the year nearing his first title shot, but if he can take down another former champion in JiYí Procházka on Nov. 21, he'll end the year near the top of the light heavyweight contenders short list. -- Waters

14. Thad Jean

PFL welterweight champion

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

The PFL has asked several figures to be the "face of the company" over the years with mixed results. Recently much of that promotional expectation has been heaped on Jean, the 28-year-old who won the 2025 welterweight tournament. Jean has legitimate skills and highlight-reel potential. He's styled on the opponents he should have, and has proven his world-class merit with hard-fought wins over tougher opponents such as Logan Storley and Jason Jackson. -- Okamoto

15. Gabriel Bonfim

UFC welterweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 21

Bonfim is another fighter on this list who could be nearing a title shot. He only has competed once this year, but was dominant in a five-round unanimous decision win over former welterweight champion Belal Muhammad. All three judges scored the fight 50-45 for Bonfirm, who claimed the No. 7 spot in ESPN's divisional rankings as a result. Bonfim's biggest hurdle going forward will be the rise in competition in a stacked 170-pound division. His next test will come against No. 6-ranked Sean Brady on Nov. 7. -- Waters

16. Salahdine Parnasse

UFC lightweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

It's been an interesting year for Parnasse. In January, he defended his lightweight championship in the Polish fight promotion KSW, winning by knockout. He vacated that title to fight on the first MMA card for Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions brand. Parnasse scored a first-round knockout over Kenneth Cross on the undercard of the most-watched MMA event ever. Last month he made his UFC debut, scoring another knockout -- his sixth in a row. The first-round finish of Dan Hooker doesn't make Parnasse a contender, but he's someone to keep watching. -- Wagenheim

17. Ateba Gautier

UFC middleweight

Age: 24

Last year's rank: NR

Gautier is an absolute wrecking ball of a human. Nine of his 11 career wins have come by knockout, including seven in the first round. Potential? Off the charts. Momentum? Undeniable. The only question around Gautier isn't about him, but his opposition. His five UFC opponents have a 4-14 combined record inside the Octagon. That will change when he meets Roman Kopylov (15-5) this weekend at UFC 332. If Gautier knocks out Kopylov, his hype will be validated. -- Okamoto

18. Erin Blanchfield

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 11

Blanchfield has been included on ESPN's list of top young prospects nearly every year since she signed with the UFC in 2021. She was ESPN's No. 1 prospect under 25 in 2023, but missed the cut the following year after suffering a one-sided drubbing to Manon Fiorot. She bounced back from that loss with back-to-back wins over Rose Namajunas and Tracy Cortez and is scheduled to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17 in a battle of top-10 flyweights. -- Waters

19. Payton Talbott

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 20

You know a young fighter is someone the UFC considers a rising prospect when you start to see him booked against championship-decorated opponents. Talbott is coming off a December win that was convincing enough to send former two-division titlist Henry Cejudo into retirement. This weekend at UFC 332, Talbott will take on another former belt-holder, Deiveson Figueiredo. These kinds of fights draw attention, even when they're against faded stars. If Talbott is successful again, he could be on his way toward ranked opposition and a slow, steady build. -- Wagenheim

20. Lone'er Kavanagh

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: NR

He can't live on one performance forever, but Kavanagh's five-round victory over former champion Brandon Moreno in February -- in Mexico, on short notice -- said a lot about this 27-year-old's capabilities. He's 1-2 in his past three appearances, but Kavanagh has a tantalizing amount of potential. How big would a Joshua Van vs. Lone'er Kavanagh title fight be, if Kavanagh were to get on a roll and give England a shot at its next UFC champion? -- Okamoto

21. Paul Hughes

PFL lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 16

Hughes came up short in two attempts to take the PFL lightweight championship from Nurmagomedov last year. Despite losing both fights by decision, Hughes proved himself to be one of the best lightweights in the world. He has been out of action this year due to a knee injury, but now that Nurmagomedov is a free agent, there's a chance for Hughes to challenge for the PFL title again immediately upon returning to active status. -- Waters

22. Gable Steveson

UFC heavyweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: NR

Steveson was about 12 seconds from being a whole lot higher on this list. As an Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was as highly anticipated a prospect as the sport has seen when he transitioned to MMA last year. After winning his first four pro fights by first-round knockout, including his UFC debut in July, Steveson looked like a heavyweight with which to be reckoned. He still might turn into that guy, but getting KO'd by the second punch heavy underdog Sean Sharaf threw at him at UFC 331 two weeks ago put the brakes on the Steveson hype train. The big dude has work to do. -- Wagenheim

23. Muhammad Mokaev

Brave CF men's flyweight champion

Age: 26

2025 rank: 27

One of the most unique -- and frustrating -- careers in MMA continues to play out outside the UFC. It's now been 26 months since Mokaev parted ways with the promotion. It's worth noting that Mokaev's last fight in the UFC was a victory over Manel Kape, who is widely expected to be the next title challenger for Van. Will we ever see a day when Mokaev can return? At the moment, there doesn't seem to be much of a thaw from the UFC side. But Mokaev is still 26 years old and still unbeaten. He's so young and freakishly good that it's impossible to count out any opportunity forever. -- Okamoto

24. Valter Walker

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Walker has been the epitome of a one-trick fighter so far in his UFC career. But if his one trick isn't broken, why fix it? Since losing by unanimous decision in his UFC debut in 2024, Walker has been on an absolute tear, beating each of his past five opponents by first-round submission. Four of those finishes have come via heel hook. It wasn't until his most recent victory over Thomas Petersen that the submission ace had to show more of his ability, transitioning from his signature heel hook attempt into a calf slicer submission for the finish. -- Waters

25. David Martinez

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Look no further than the UFC's matchmaking to decipher how promising Martinez is. The UFC tried to pair him with Umar Nurmagomedov in July, but Martinez was forced to withdraw because of injury. He has quietly taken out some of the most respected veterans in the bantamweight division -- Dan Ige, Marlon Vera and Rob Font -- over the past 12 months and is on the cusp of a top-five ranking. Martinez lacks some of the star power of other names on this list, but he's likely to draw big-name opponents in the near future. Consistent results would inevitably skyrocket every aspect of his career. -- Okamoto

26. Tommy McMillen

UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

McMillen, who trains with former UFC men's bantamweight champion Sean O'Malley, has had a breakout performance this year. He earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" a year ago and has strung together three straight wins since. He was tested in his most recent bout, a unanimous decision win over Marwan Rahiki, but he outpointed Rahiki on all three of the judges' scorecards. He's earned the right to take a step up in competition in his next Octagon appearance. -- Waters

27. Jose Miguel Delgado
UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Delgado was victorious in four of his first five trips to the Octagon before running into Jean Silva in the main event of Noche UFC last month. Fighting on short notice, Delgado lost by third-round submission, but he won the first round and held his own until running low on energy, whereupon Silva took over. His success in the early rounds gives Delgado building blocks for the future. -- Wagenheim

28. Raul Rosas Jr.

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 21

2025 rank: 30

Still just 21 years old, Rosas is 7-1 in the UFC -- and the context around some of those wins is starting to grow. No longer is Rosas a phenom teenager operating on UFC prelims. Coming off his first UFC main event on Sept. 26, Rosas now holds two significant wins over proven veterans in Rob Font and Raoni Barcelos and is a ranked UFC bantamweight ... all before his 22nd birthday next week. There is no comparison to Rosas when it comes to experience gained at such a young age. There are plenty of steps between where he is now and a UFC championship, but he's certainly on the right path. -- Okamoto

29. Baisangur Susurkaev

UFC middleweight

Age: 25

2025 rank: 25

Susurkaev, a longtime training partner of former champion Khamzat Chimaev, made a name for himself last summer when he earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" then made his official debut four days later at UFC 319. He finished both of his opponents in those contests. In his lone appearance this year, Susurkaev picked up another finish, beating Djorden Santos by third-round submission in May. Next, he'll take on a fellow unbeaten prospect Donte Johnson at UFC 334 in November. A win over Johnson could establish Susurkaev as a future problem for top middleweight fighters. -- Waters

30. Iasmin Lucindo

UFC strawweight

Age: 24

2025 rank: 29

Lucindo had won five of six fights and was on the rise before an injury and a failed drug test in September 2025 derailed her. She withdrew from a fight with strawweight contender Gillian Robertson and ended up being suspended for a year, while Robertson went on to a title challenge. Lucindo is eligible to compete again, and at 24 years old she has time to build herself back up to contendership in the 115-pound division. -- Wagenheim

stories.headline: Roosters reveal stance on pre-GF break amid Watson blow
stories.summary: Trent Robinson has resisted the urge to join growing calls for the NRL to introduce a two-week break before the grand final, despite Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson failing to clear concussion protocols to take the field.
stories.body:
Trent Robinson has resisted the urge to join growing calls for the NRL to introduce a two-week break before the Grand Final, despite Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson failing to clear concussion protocols to take the field.

The Roosters attempted to have Watson cleared to play in Sunday's season decider after he suffering a head knock during his side's preliminary final win over the Dolphins.

Under NRL concussion guidelines, players cannot return to play inside 11 days and despite responding well, Watson was pulled from the Roosters' squad on Friday after meeting with specialists.

Many pundits this week have argued for a fortnight's break between the preliminary finals and the Grand Final, which would have given Watson the chance to line up in his final Roosters game before joining St George Illawarra.

But Robinson said he was not in favour of such a move.

"These are unfortunate things that happen, but we have protocols for a reason," the Roosters coach said at Accor Stadium on Saturday.

"I'm more for the week off before the finals than I am before the Grand Final.

"I feel like momentum's built throughout the final series and the attrition part of it is a part of our game."

Watson, who will be replaced in Robinson's 19-man squad by hooker Benaiah Ioelu, becomes the first player to miss a Grand Final due to the concussion since the NRL implemented new rules at the start of the 2023 season.

The 30-year-old, who spent four seasons with Newcastle, is one of the Roosters' most popular characters and was informed of his exclusion from the Grand Final squad during training on Friday.

"Connor's a good man, a strong man, he's his own man, and so he had to sort of control all that -- he knew we were in the middle of a session," Robinson said.

"The absolute devastation that it is for him, all the work that's gone into his career for him and his family and friends -- then you get the news like that (and) it's quite tough.

"But then he spoke to the group quite clearly about (how) this is about the group.

"Then the player that took his spot in the 19, Benaiah, spoke about the love for Connor and what it means for his role coming into the team."

Robinson is aiming to win a fourth premiership at the club, having last tasted Grand Final glory seven years ago.

Five members of the 2019 premiership-winning squad remain, with a young core, headlined by 24-year-old halfback Sam Walker, gunning to win their first NRL title.

Veteran five-eighth Daly Cherry-Evans will partner Walker, who Robinson described as a "free spirit".

"He's quite young for a half the age that he is, and he's been moulding his game," Robinson said.

"We've been moulding our team to his game and it takes some time and we're ready.

stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

Friday, October 2

Charles Leclerc tops second practice, Mercedes off the pace

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

Trending rumors

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

- Juventus have declared that Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic are "untouchable" in future transfer markets, with the club keen to build around the pair, reports La Gazzetta. Yildiz, 21, has previously attracted interest from Arsenal and Real Madrid, having shown plenty of potential. The forward ended up staying with Juventus over the summer, though a recent injury issue means he will be out until December. As for Alajbegovic, the Bianconeri managed to beat plenty of competition to his signature from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer transfer window. With the 19-year-old forward featuring for the club since, and reports of potential interest from the likes of Chelsea in the future, Juventus have set a clear stance of no exit for now.

- Arsenal continue to track a move for Junior Kroupi, with PSG also following proceedings for the Bournemouth forward, who is ramping up his recovery from an injury that has prevented him from playing this season. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: Toby Greene joins Geelong on day one of AFL free agency
stories.summary: The AFL has revealed Greater Western Sydney's compensation draft pick after former skipper Toby Greene completed his late-career move to Geelong.
stories.body:
Toby Greene has become the first major AFL free agency domino to fall, with Greater Western Sydney to receive a second-round draft pick for losing their former captain to Geelong.

The Cats lodged paperwork on Friday to land the inaugural Giant as an unrestricted free agent.

Greene, a triple All Australian and dual club champion, booted 450 goals across his 15-year, 282-game tenure for GWS.

The 33-year-old cited family reasons for returning to his native Victoria and reunites with his close mate and former Giants forward Jeremy Cameron at the Cattery on a lucrative three-year deal.

The Giants will receive a second round draft selection as compensation, currently slated at No.26.

Earlier, key forward Joel Amartey's switch from Sydney to Carlton was confirmed as the free agency period opened.

The Swans will receive draft compensation for losing the unrestricted 27-year-old, who was an emergency during finals after failing to convince coach Dean Cox following a partial Achilles tear.

Paperwork will be lodged later on Friday to rubber stamp Lachie Neale's move to Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent after the Brisbane Lions star added a third premiership medal to his swag of silverware.

Melbourne's 2021 premiership vice-captain Jack Viney is poised for a move with two years remaining on his contract after meeting with West Coast.

After being sidelined through injury for all but one game this season, the 32-year-old was told by coach Steven King there would likely be limited opportunities for him in the Demons midfield.

"Footy's gone that way mate," Viney told 10 News at Perth Airport on Thursday.

"So took a bit to process early days, but we're here now, so we'll make the best of the opportunity ... it (a deal) will get done."

Young Hawthorn forward Calsher Dear, meanwhile, has opted to stay at the Hawks on a two-year deal after weighing up a potential move to the Dees.

The 21-year-old, son of late 1991 Norm Smith medallist Paul Dear, burst onto the scene in his debut season with 25 goals from 17 appearances in 2024.

But the emerging tall has struggled to hold his spot through injury and internal competition, adding just 14 games in 2025 and 2026.

"We are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond," Hawks list manager Mark McKenzie said.

Hawthorn's key forward selection squeeze is set to worsen in 2027, with Gold Coast's restricted free agent Ben King expected to join Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis, Mabior Chol and Dear.

stories.headline: Mason McTavish scores right away in Blues debut in a 4-0 opening-night win over Stars
stories.summary: — Mason McTavish scored only 94 seconds into his first game with the Blues to put them ahead to stay, Joel Hofer stopped 25 shots for his ninth career shutout and St. Louis won 4-0 at...
stories.body:
DALLAS -- — Mason McTavish scored only 94 seconds into his first game with the Blues to put them ahead to stay, Joel Hofer stopped 25 shots for his ninth career shutout and St. Louis won 4-0 at Dallas on Friday night in the season opener for both teams.


Dalibor Dvorsky scored in the second period for the Blues before they got empty-netters from Jimmy Snuggerud and Pius Suter in the game's final 2 1/2 minutes.


The 21-year-old Dvorsky had his open shot at the net when goalie Jake Oettinger fell down after getting clipped by teammate Roope Hintz. Oettinger stopped 20 shots.


Dallas lost a season opener for the first time since 2019, ending a six-game winning streak that had been the NHL's longest active streak. The Stars were also shut out in a home opener for the first time since moving to Dallas before the 1993-94 season.


Dallas and St. Louis were among seven teams to play their first game Friday, three nights after the NHL season began.


Hofer had six shutouts in 43 starts for the Blues last season.


McTavish was traded from Anaheim to St. Louis for two first-round picks (Nos. 15 and 29) during the draft in June. He scored the fifth-quickest goal to start a season opener in Blues franchise history.


Blues defenseman Brandon Carlo got a game misconduct for a kneeing penalty early in the third period that sent top-line center Hintz, in his first game since March 6, down to the ice while grabbing at his left knee.


Hintz, who tore his hamstring in two places last season, was moving gingerly when behind helped off the ice, but returned a few minutes later.


Blues forward Alexey Toropchenko left with an apparent right shoulder injury early in the second period after he was hit behind his net by Lian Bichsel and Tyler Seguin.


Up next
Both teams play again Saturday. St. Louis is at Colorado, and Dallas plays in Nashville.

stories.headline: Guardians, White Sox renew AL Central rivalry as Division Series opens in Cleveland
stories.summary: — Stephen Vogt and Will Venable don't need to pore over extra scouting reports as the Cleveland Guardians get set to host the Chicago White Sox in Saturday's Game 1 of the AL Division Series.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Stephen Vogt and Will Venable don't need to pore over extra scouting reports as the Cleveland Guardians get set to host the Chicago White Sox in Saturday's Game 1 of the AL Division Series.


The AL Central rivals last faced each other two weeks ago, when the Guardians took two of three and moved into the division lead. Cleveland ended up winning its third straight division title and 14th since 1995.


Chicago won the season series 7-6 after Cleveland took 11 of 13 in 2025.


It's the third straight year the Guardians will open the postseason against a division opponent. They faced Detroit in the 2024 Division Series and in the Wild Card Series last year.


“There’s a little bit of a rivalry there because all three years that’s who you’ve been racing with to get in. There’s emotion. There’s a lot of things that make this series really exciting,” said Vogt, Cleveland's manager. “I do think there’s no secrets. We know them. They know us. So it’s just go out and execute and let’s see who can win three games before the other team.”


Venable pointed out that only one run separated the teams this season. Chicago had a 58-57 edge.


“I mean, it really has been crazy kind of the back and forth that we’ve had all year. So we’re excited about the opportunity to play these guys, but we know full well how challenging it is to beat them,” the White Sox manager said.


Chicago comes in with momentum after its two-game Wild Card Series sweep at Houston. Nine players made their postseason debuts in that series, including second baseman Chase Meidroth and catcher Kyle Teel. Meidroth went 4 for 7 with a homer and four RBI against the Astros, while Teel was 3 for 10. Teel also was successful on all five of his ABS challenges behind the plate.


Cleveland (85-77) has the third-youngest lineup in the American League and used 145 different batting orders this season. Depending on final roster decisions, the Guardians could have as many as seven players making their postseason debut, including Jo Adell, who was acquired from the Los Angeles Angels near the trade deadline.


Rookie matchup in Game 1
Both teams will send rookies to the mound in Game 1 with Chicago’s Hagen Smith opposing Cleveland’s Parker Messick. According to Sportradar, it will be the 23rd postseason game in which both teams used a rookie starting pitcher.


Chicago will begin the series with a bullpen game. Smith will be the opener again after throwing three scoreless innings in Tuesday’s 6-3 victory at Houston in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series.


Smith (3-3, 1.29 ERA) made three appearances against Cleveland in the regular season, going 1-1 with a 3.18 ERA. The left-hander allowed the go-ahead run during the sixth inning of Cleveland’s 6-3 victory on Sept. 16 that moved the Guardians into the AL Central lead.


“I think he gives us a really good shot up front here. I do feel like we can lean on some of the bullpen arms to get us through some bulk here and Hagen is as good as any for us,” Venable said.


Messick (12-9, 2.56 ERA) will go against the White Sox for the fifth time this season. The left-hander is 2-1 with a 2.81 ERA and has won his last two starts against Chicago.


“Every lineup you’re going to face is pretty good. And I’ve got just as much information on them as they do on me, so I think it’s just best stuff on best stuff and whoever executes more pitches is going to win and whoever hits more mistakes is going to win,” Messick said.


Vogt could tell the White Sox would be better this year
The heartiest of White Sox fans, including Pope Leo XIV, could have envisioned their dramatic turnaround from three consecutive 100-loss seasons to winning their first postseason series in 21 years.


Vogt saw signs beginning last season that Chicago's rebuild would take root.


“I thought they had some really good players last year but records don’t always tell the full story of a team. You could tell at spring training (this year) this is going to be a different team. What they’ve done putting it together has been really cool,” Vogt said.


Guardians' offense back on track
Cleveland is batting .255 since the Aug. 3 trade deadline, second-best in the American League. The Guardians were 14th with a .231 average before adding Adell and Nathaniel Lowe. Adell had a team-leading 32 RBI since coming to the Guardians while Lowe drove in 27, including a big league-best eight sacrifice flies.


Steven Kwan's .353 batting average since the All-Star break was best in the majors.


White Sox bring the home run power
While Cleveland was the only team in the majors without a batter who hit 20 home runs, Chicago had three with at least 30. Japanese rookie slugger Munetaka Murakami led the way with 35, followed by Miguel Vargas (33) and Colson Montgomery (31).


Vargas went 14 of 46 with three homers and 10 RBI against the Guardians this season. Montgomery also had three homers but was 9 of 47, and Murakami went 3 of 19 while going deep twice.

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Oct. 2

Hawkins, Grizzlies mutually agree to part ways
The Memphis Grizzlies and guard Jordan Hawkins have agreed to part ways via waivers, allowing the 2023 lottery pick to find a new home in free agency, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The move comes three weeks after arriving as part of a four-player trade with the New Orleans Pelicans for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to preview the NBA's Pacific Division, including the biggest questions for the Los Angeles Lakers, Golden State Warriors and the rest of the division. Slater on the Warriors' options this season: "I think we mentioned it last time we talked about the Warriors, but think about what the Lakers did with LeBron. I know we just questioned some of the deals they signed, but the fact that they could sign all those deals was because LeBron James took all his money and walked away. So you could let Jimmy [Butler] somewhat walk away.

"The other thing is, Jimmy and the Warriors really are fond of each other and we'll see what he looks like when he does come back. Obviously Jimmy's going to want every dollar he can get, but there's a chance Jimmy and Draymond [Green] could take pay cuts next season, right? The market might demand that they do.

"Jimmy fits really well with Steph Curry. We've seen that. Draymond is another player that you're going to hear a lot of noise about in the first week of camp from the Warriors about shifting Draymond's role and some of the numbers last year. With Draymond and Steph Curry on the floor together, it was still plus-105 last year, still a good offensive rating,117.7, but the moment Steph's been off the floor, and last year he was off the floor a lot, their offense cratered when Draymond was on the floor and was actually OK when it was no Draymond and no Steph.

"I've had these conversations with Steve [Kerr] and again I think you're going to hear it a lot publicly in their messaging, they're going to adapt the offense at times away from Draymond. They're going to try to make him more of a spot-up shooter at times instead of giving him the ball. They're trying to limit his turnovers."
